in_sanskrit.name: वरद
in_sanskrit.meaning: blessing, boon, mercy, grace, benevolence, gift
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: वरद् (varad) is a Sanskrit word that means blessing, boon, mercy, grace, benevolence, and gift. It is derived from the Sanskrit root वृ (vṛ), which means 'to rain', and the suffix द (da), which means 'giver'. In Hindu mythology, Varad is also the name of a form of Vishnu, who is the giver of blessings and boons.

in_hindi.name: वारद
in_hindi.long_meaning: वारद (vārad) is the Hindi name for the Sanskrit word वरद् (varad). It is pronounced as 'vā-rad'. The meaning of the name is 'better, superior, excellent, or superior to others'. In Hinduism, Varad is also a name of Lord Vishnu, who is the giver of blessings and boons.

vedic_reference.note: Varad is a Sanskrit word and a name of Lord Vishnu in Hindu mythology. It is derived from the Sanskrit root वृ (vṛ), which means 'to rain', and the suffix द (da), which means 'giver'. In the Rigveda, Varad is mentioned as a name of Indra, the god of rain. However, in later Hindu texts, Varad becomes synonymous with Lord Vishnu, who is the giver of blessings and boons.
